ux: check (and a Check button) · hint · solution · task · reset · clear · help

immersive_cli_coach (action + level + step index only, never command text)
immersive_cli_review_card (sim + task + step index + why: solution | check-fail — never command text)
immersive_cli_voice (sim + kind: verb | command | none | error + ok — never the transcript)
cli.storage: localStorage il.immersiveCli.v1 (task completions + best command count, device only); CLI review cards in il.immersiveReview.v1 (device only)
cli.honesty: Simulated shell over the in-browser rules engine — real CLI syntax, computed output (kubectl/etcdctl/aws-shaped, not byte-identical). Not a real shell, container, cluster, AWS account or hosted lab fleet. Unmodelled commands say so instead of inventing output.

diagnosis: out of order (seen before the previous step verified)
right command family, wrong cluster state

coach.honesty: Deterministic rules over the same in-browser sim state — not an LLM, not reading a real terminal, knows only what the drill models.

cli.gatewayNote: Gateway API pack (2026-10-21) drives the gateway-api sim on the same authored ingress-gateway.glb. GatewayClass lab-gw (controllerName example.net/lab-gateway-controller) is a lab implementation computed by the rules engine — not Envoy Gateway, Istio, Cilium or NGINX Gateway Fabric, and not a live Gateway.
cli.nodeNote: Worker-node pack (2026-10-22) drives node-troubleshoot on the NEW authored node-troubleshoot.glb. systemd, journald, crictl, df and sed output is computed from sim state (shaped like the real tools, not byte-identical; journal lines are labelled representative). No VM, no real kubelet, no clock: durations such as node-monitor-grace-period and the 300s eviction toleration are explained, not simulated.
cli.serviceDnsNote: Service + DNS pack (2026-10-23) drives service-dns on the NEW authored service-dns.glb. Lookups go through the rules engine's resolv.conf model (search shop.svc.cluster.local svc.cluster.local cluster.local, ndots:5) over four cluster records; nslookup / dig / CoreDNS log output is shaped like the real tools (labelled representative), not byte-identical. No live cluster, no real CoreDNS, no internet upstream, no clock: CrashLoopBackOff back-off and resolver timeouts are explained, not counted down. Files written with `>` live only in this terminal session.
cli.cniNote: CNI pack (2026-10-27) drives cni-network on the authored cni-pod-network.glb (no new asset). Calico is the modelled CNI; calico.yaml and new-pool.yaml are trimmed lab stand-ins, and kubectl get/patch ippool stands in for calicoctl or the Calico API server (projectcalico.org/v3). The pool migration follows Calico's documented order (create the new pool, disable the old one, recreate pods). ping / curl / nslookup results are computed from the rules engine, shaped like busybox and curl output, not byte-identical. No live cluster, no real Calico, no VPC routing, no clock.
cli.meshNote: Service-mesh pack (2026-10-27) drives mesh-mtls on the authored service-mesh-sidecar.glb (no new asset). Istio semantics: STRICT resets plaintext clients, injection needs the namespace label and newly created pods, PERMISSIVE accepts both, istiod at zero leaves existing sidecars on their last config while the sidecar-injector webhook (failurePolicy Fail) blocks new pods. payments echoes headers like httpbin /headers, so X-Forwarded-Client-Cert shows an mTLS hop. istioctl output is computed and trimmed. Not CKA core; no live mesh, no real Envoy or istiod.
cli.cksNote: CKS pack (2026-10-29) drives cks-pod-security on the NEW authored cks-pod-security.glb. PodSecurity admission messages follow the built-in controller's format (violates PodSecurity "restricted:latest": …); /proc status, id, curl and the audit.k8s.io/v1 event are computed from sim state and labelled representative where shaped, not byte-identical. No live cluster, no real kubelet, kernel or seccomp, no clock: the static-pod restart after a manifest edit is explained, not waited for. The audit event shows that a Metadata-level rule never logs the Secret's data.
cli.supplyChainNote: CKS supply-chain pack (2026-11-02) drives cks-supply-chain on the NEW authored cks-supply-chain.glb. The ValidatingAdmissionPolicy denial follows the documented "ValidatingAdmissionPolicy '…' with binding '…' denied request" format; trivy tables, the CycloneDX SBOM, cosign verify/attest output and the Kyverno-style verifyImages denial are computed from sim state and labelled representative, not byte-identical. Only CRITICAL findings are modelled (CVE-2023-45853 in zlib1g on a debian:bookworm base). No registry, no CI runner, no real trivy, cosign, Rekor or Kyverno, no clock.
cli.runtimeNote: CKS runtime pack (2026-11-03) drives cks-runtime-security on the NEW authored cks-runtime-security.glb. The lab box is node01 with an admin kubeconfig (a real worker would not have one). Falco output, the lab rule "Shell in container" (a custom local rule with no tty requirement, not Falco's default "Terminal shell in container"), aa-status, apparmor_parser, CreateContainerError events, touch errors (Permission denied vs Read-only file system) and the audit.k8s.io/v1 pods/exec event are computed from sim state and labelled representative, not byte-identical. No live cluster, no real Falco, kernel, eBPF probe or AppArmor, no clock: Falco's rules reload and the kubelet's retry after the profile loads are explained, not waited for.
cli.hardeningNote: CKS CIS-benchmark pack (2026-11-04) drives cks-cluster-hardening on the NEW authored cks-cluster-hardening.glb. The lab box is the controlplane node of a kubeadm cluster, which also runs a kubelet, so both kube-bench targets apply there. kube-bench output uses the check ids and texts of aquasecurity/kube-bench cfg/cis-1.12 (1.1.11, 1.2.15, 4.2.1, 4.2.2, 4.2.4 — 4.2.4 is Manual, so it reports WARN) trimmed to those five checks; kubelet responses (PodList / Forbidden (user=…, verb=get, resource=nodes, subresource=proxy) / Unauthorized), curl errors, stat, systemctl and the config files are computed from sim state and labelled representative, not byte-identical. A sed pattern that would also flip webhook token authentication is refused with an explanation. No live cluster, no real kube-bench, kubelet, etcd or systemd, no clock: the kubelet restart and the static-pod re-creation are explained, not waited for.

cks_coverage.curriculum: cncf/curriculum CKS v1.34: Cluster Setup 15% · Cluster Hardening 15% · System Hardening 10% · Minimize Microservice Vulnerabilities 20% · Supply Chain Security 20% · Monitoring, Logging and Runtime Security 20%

covered.Cluster Setup: NetworkPolicy default-deny / allow (cks-pod-security + netpol-isolation); CIS benchmark with kube-bench: kubelet anonymous auth, AlwaysAllow vs Webhook, read-only port, restart after a config edit, etcd data dir permissions, API server profiling (cks-cluster-hardening)
covered.Cluster Hardening: RBAC least privilege for ServiceAccounts (cks-pod-security + rbac-authz)
covered.System Hardening: seccomp RuntimeDefault vs Unconfined (cks-pod-security); AppArmor Localhost profiles: load with apparmor_parser, CreateContainerError when missing, deny-write (cks-runtime-security)
covered.Monitoring, Logging & Runtime Security: API server audit policy + log backend (cks-pod-security); Falco runtime detection, rule overrides, immutable containers (readOnlyRootFilesystem), audit vs runtime visibility (cks-runtime-security)
covered.Supply Chain Security: allowed registries (ValidatingAdmissionPolicy), Trivy scan gate + minimal base image, CycloneDX SBOM, cosign signing + admission signature verification, digest pinning (cks-supply-chain)

notCovered: static analysis of manifests (kubesec / KubeLinter) and keyless (Sigstore OIDC) signing
Falco rule authoring beyond one lab rule, Falcosidekick / alert routing, Tetragon / Tracee
kube-bench checks beyond the five modelled (file ownership/permissions of manifests and PKI, controller-manager and scheduler flags, kubelet TLS / rotation)
